Frequently Asked Questions (Supabase vs Neon Branching Calc)

How does Neon database branching differ from Supabase branching?

Neon uses a copy-on-write storage engine where each preview branch shares pages with the parent database until modified. This means creating a branch takes less than 1 second, consumes near-zero storage, and scales to zero when idle. Supabase branching runs a logical branch with dedicated compute add-ons ($0.32/branch/day = ~$9.60/mo each), which can add up with frequent preview deployments.

Can Neon databases truly scale to zero?

Yes. Neon serverless compute decouples storage from compute and automatically suspends compute endpoints after a configurable period of inactivity (default 5 minutes). When an incoming SQL query or connection arrives via the Neon Serverless Driver or connection pooler, it cold-starts in 300ms–500ms, reducing staging and PR preview compute costs to near $0.

When is Supabase more cost-effective than Neon?

Supabase is often more cost-effective if you heavily utilize its integrated ecosystem beyond core PostgreSQL: built-in Row Level Security (RLS) Auth, Supabase Storage (S3-compatible object storage), Realtime WebSocket subscriptions, Edge Functions, and pgvector embeddings included in the $25/mo Pro tier.
